title: FROM TERROR TO A BETTER MEDIATOR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Israelites said to Moses, "We will die! We are lost, we are all lost! Anyone who even comes near the tabernacle of the Lord will die. Are we all going to die?" — Num 17:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends on a note of raw fear. Having witnessed God's holiness in judgment and now in the budding staff, the people cry out in dread: "We will die! We are all lost!" They have grasped, perhaps for the first time, how holy and unapproachable God is, and it terrifies them. To come near Him seems to mean death.

We should not dismiss their fear, because it contains real truth. A holy God cannot simply be approached casually by sinful people. The people were right that, left to themselves, they could not stand in His presence and live. This is a sober recognition that many today have lost — the sheer, weighty holiness of God, before whom sinners cannot presume to stroll.

But their cry, though it grasps God's holiness, misses His provision. They saw the danger of coming near, but not yet the God-given way to come near safely. They cried "we are all lost" as though there were no hope, when in fact God had already given them a priesthood, a tabernacle, and a system of atonement precisely so they could dwell near Him and live. Their terror needed to be met with the mediator God had provided.

And here the whole book of Numbers strains forward to Christ. The people's despairing question — "Are we all going to die?" — finds its answer not in a budding staff or an earthly priest, but in Jesus. He is the mediator who bridges the gulf between a holy God and lost sinners. Through Him we may now "approach God's throne of grace with confidence." The terror of the tabernacle gives way to the welcome of the cross. Because our great High Priest has made atonement, we need not cry "we are lost." In Christ, we may draw near and live.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you lost a sense of the weighty holiness of God?
2. Why is fear of God's holiness incomplete without His provision to draw near?
3. How does Jesus, your mediator, turn terror into confident welcome?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, restore in me a right sense of Your holiness, and thank You that You have not left me lost. Thank You for Jesus, my mediator, through whom I can approach Your throne of grace with confidence. In Him I draw near and live. Amen.
